name: Greenock
reason: barossa.com Barossa Towns page and itinerary "Explore Greenock" name the heritage village; Historical Walk of Greenock lists 27 sites, plus the Heysen-side aviation museum. A village a guide recommends as a stop.

name: Springton
reason: barossa.com town page and southaustralia.com list the Herbig Family Tree (free, ~500-year-old hollow red gum where the settler family lived) and Friedensberg school museum. Village draw is the tree; bio should say so.

name: Eden Valley
reason: barossa.com itinerary "Explore Eden Valley" names Eden Valley Scenic Lookout (Burke's Hill), main-street silhouettes and the high-country village. Against: much of the draw is cellar doors. Second-tier village stop.

name: Mallala
reason: Searched Wikivoyage, SA tourism, council: only the Mallala Motor Sport Park (event-day circuit), a war memorial and an equestrian centre. No permanent visitor draw; not a spot.

name: Watervale
reason: Searched clarevalley.com.au and southaustralia.com: only the village, National Trust buildings seen from outside, cellar doors and the Riesling Trail (listed separately). Nothing to do for half an hour.

name: Penwortham
reason: southaustralia.com/clarevalley.com.au list John Horrocks Cottage, open only the first Sunday of the month or by appointment, plus a village walk and cellar doors; not there whenever a visitor arrives.

name: Saddleworth
reason: southaustralia.com destination page only; a 3 km heritage walk, a small museum and a hotel. No distinct named draw found.

name: Balaklava
reason: Town listing only (southaustralia.com, clarevalley.com.au). Draws are part-time museum (2nd/4th Sunday), Rocks Reserve and Devils Gardens, none named as a stop by a guide; the town is not itself a draw.

name: Snowtown
reason: southaustralia.com page names the wind farm viewed from the highway and the Big Blade on display (a 10-minute look); Lake Bumbunga is listed separately. Town not a draw.

name: Blyth
reason: southaustralia.com lists three permanent stops in Blyth: the Blyth Mosaic, the 4.4 km Dean Nicolle Eucalypt Walk (~300 eucalypt species) and nearby Brooks Lookout (90 km view to Yorke Peninsula). Small, but enough to fill 30+ min.

name: Farrell Flat
reason: Duplicate of Farrell Flat Silo Art; the town wrapper adds nothing a guide names.

name: Jamestown
reason: southaustralia.com lists Jamestown under Flinders Ranges and Outback: Memorial Park (Krupp cannon), Diggers Walk, RM Williams Story, railway museum; nothing a guide singles out as a stop and no Clare-region source. Searched southaustralia.com, Apollo guide.

name: Barossa Museum
reason: Wikivoyage See and barossa.com list the local-history museum in the Old Telegraph Station, Tanunda, a stop on the Tanunda Heritage Trail. Against: hours are limited (opening days conflict between listings).

name: Barossa Trail
reason: Searched barossa.com and southaustralia.com; only the Barossa by Bike map and unnamed cycle routes. No distinct named trail with a counted source.

name: Lyndoch Recreation Park
reason: Searched web, parks.sa.gov.au, barossa.com: nothing found naming it as somewhere to go; local reserve.

name: Château Tanunda
reason: For: grand 1890 chateau open daily with 40-min cellar tours and croquet lawn; Wikivoyage and southaustralia.com list it. Against: both list it as a winery/cellar door, which the rules exclude unless a recognised attraction.

name: Jacob's Creek Visitor Centre
reason: For: barossa.com and Wikivoyage list it; self-guided Trail of Discovery creek walk and demonstration vineyard make a 30+ min stop at a famous brand. Against: it is a cellar door/visitor centre of a winery.

name: Yalumba
reason: Cellar door of a winery (Wikivoyage Drink listing); tours conflict across sources. Not a distinct visitor place under the winery exclusion. Searched Time Out, Expedia.

name: Henschke
reason: Wikivoyage lists it under Wineries; a cellar door. Hill of Grace is a private vineyard. Business, not a spot.

name: Barossa Range
reason: Landform; searched barossa.com and southaustralia.com, no visitor source names anything to do there (Menglers Hill Lookout is the named stop).

name: Auburn Wine Walk
reason: Searched clarevalley.com.au and southaustralia.com: no counted source found; cellar-door walk.

name: Neagles Rock Short Walk
reason: 1 km, 45-minute loop to a 455 m lookout with rare remnant woodland; named on clarevalley.com.au Short Walks, southaustralia.com and Walking SA.

name: Rattler Trail
reason: 19 km walking/cycling rail trail Riverton to Auburn (joins the Riesling Trail); southaustralia.com attraction page plus Walking SA.

name: Mimbara Conservation Park
reason: Searched parks.sa.gov.au, web: only a Wikipedia article (14 sq km park near Burra); no visitor facilities or walks named.

name: Bowman Park
reason: flindersandoutback.com.au (regional tourism board) names Bowman Recreational Park near Crystal Brook: walking trails, 1850s homestead ruins and infirmary, Heysen Trail, kangaroos. Note: sits at region edge (Crystal Brook); proposer to confirm region.

name: Para Wirra Conservation Park
reason: parks.sa.gov.au names walks (Hissey Loop 1 hr, Lake Discovery Walk 30 min, Mack Creek Hike 4 hr). Note: Gawler/Adelaide fringe, proposer to resolve region.

name: Lake Bumbunga
reason: Wakefield Regional Council "10 things to see and do" and Clare Valley Tourism list the pink salt lake beside the highway at Lochiel, with a lookout and Loch-Eel sculpture. Roadside icon guides name; colour varies.

name: Redruth Gaol
reason: National Trust site in Burra open to visitors through the Burra Heritage Passport (exercise yards, cells; Breaker Morant filmed here); listed by clarevalley.com.au and southaustralia.com.

name: Hats Auburn Courthouse Cultural Centre
reason: HATS runs it as a performance venue with 25-30 events a year; visit depends on events, not a standing attraction (the CJ Dennis museum on site is a separate place). Searched clarevalley.com.au, artshub.

name: Farrell Flat Silo Art
reason: Silo mural of the last train through town (2020), first of the Clare Valley Silo Art Trail; clarevalley.com.au and southaustralia.com list it. Roadside icon, short stop.

name: Eudunda Silo Art
reason: Silo mural honouring local authors incl. Colin Thiele; on the Clare Valley Tourism Silo Art Trail page and clarevalley.com.au. Roadside icon, short stop.

name: Miners Dugouts
reason: Burra Heritage Passport key opens restored creek-bank dugouts; southaustralia.com and clarevalley.com.au passport pages name it as part of Burra's heritage trail. Short stop, second-tier.

name: Polish Hill River Church Museum
reason: clarevalley.com.au directory lists it, but the museum opens only 11am-4pm on the first Sunday of each month or by appointment (phrcm.org.au); not there whenever a visitor arrives.

name: Burra Railway Station
reason: Wikivoyage Burra See listing: former station with a museum of the town and its railway; free entry via Burra Passport. Modest second-tier stop.

name: Bon Accord Mine Complex
reason: National Trust museum on West and Linkson Streets, Burra, an interpretive centre on 1850s mining with relics and ore samples; part of Burra Passport. Distinct from Burra Mine.

name: Clare Valley Racecourse
reason: Racecourse used on event days only; searched clarevalley.com.au, no visitor listing.

name: Canowie Station
reason: Working pastoral station; searched southaustralia.com and clarevalley.com.au, no public visit offered.

name: Hummock Range
reason: Range containing wind-farm land; no visitor source names a feature to visit (Snowtown page mentions it only as the wind farm site).

name: Hornsdale Power Reserve
reason: Operating battery with no visitor access or counted visitor source; searched southaustralia.com.

name: Heysen Trail
reason: For: 1,200 km flagship walking trail with an official site (heysentrail.asn.au) and sections named in Barossa/Clare/Bowman Park pages. Against: a linear feature spanning many regions with no single access point or midpoint inside this region; placement problem, not a visitor-spot problem.

name: Mawson Trail
reason: For: ~900 km cycling trail Adelaide Hills to Blinman, promoted by tourism boards, passes the Rattler loop. Against: long linear route spanning regions; no single place in this region; I opened no agency page for it (searches returned only guides and Wikipedia).

name: Gawler National Trust Museum
reason: Wikivoyage lists only a dead link; open Tue-Fri 1-4pm normally but a July 2026 Bunyip Press report says it is closed after structural damage with no reopening date.
